script.analysis: All 19,813 stored characters read in two contiguous ranges with canonical hash match. Hook: paycheck disappears; Americans lose ~$948/year from financial illiteracy. Composite Alex (26, $55K). Fifteen Q&As: inflation (9.1% June 2022 peak, groceries +24%, ~2.4% early 2026); credit score factors and mortgage cost of fair vs excellent credit; progressive brackets (myth that raises reduce take-home) with standard deduction; why markets move (hypothetical "April 2027" tariff shock); stock ownership vs gambling, 62% own stocks, top 1% ~50%; compounding $250/month from 25 vs 35; 401k and match, participation; savings 0.39% vs index fund; good vs bad debt, card debt and APR; net worth; housing prices (record median, undersupply, lock-in, super-prime lending); how banks earn and overdraft fees; hedge funds and Buffett bet; FDIC and SVB; recessions frequency and best-days; Alex's progress and close. Clear, broad, mostly accurate, with several stale or misstated figures. No community CTA. ASR not audio-verified.

claim_audit: 0:9900 CPI peak 9.1% (June 2022) correct; food-at-home ~+24% 2020-2024 consistent; ~2.4% early-2026 inflation plausible. Credit score weights 35%/30% correct. Brackets quoted ($11,925 10% ceiling, ~$48K 12% ceiling, 37% above ~$626K, $15,750 standard deduction) are 2025 tax-year values; 2026 values are higher (~$12,400 / ~$50,400 / ~$640,600 / $16,100) - stale but labeled "current guidelines". A raise never reduces take-home under brackets - correct (ignoring benefit cliffs). The "hypothetical April 2027" tariff shock ($5.8T loss, 9% one-day gain) mirrors actual April 2025 events, oddly framed as hypothetical. ~62% of adults own stocks (Gallup) and top 1% ~50% of equities (Fed DFA) consistent. $250/month at 8% from 25 vs 35 to 65: ~$873K vs ~$373K - correct. 2026 401k limit is $24,500, not $24,000. $60K x 6% = $3,600 + $1,800 match correct. "Only 52% of workers with access use it" conflates overall participation (~half of all workers) with take-up among those with access (~three-quarters per BLS).

9900:19813 $10,000 for 20 years at 0.39% = ~$10,810 vs 10% = ~$67,275 - correct. Card debt ~$1.28T consistent. "90% of millionaires built their wealth through real estate" is a misattributed popular quote, unsupported by wealth surveys. Median home price record ~$435-446K (2025) consistent; "$2,000/month with 20% down" understates P&I at ~6.5% (~$2,250). Housing undersupply estimates range widely (1-5M); 1.2M is the low end. Overdraft revenue ~$5-6B consistent with CFPB. Buffett bet: $1M in the index gaining ~$854K vs funds-of-funds ~$220K consistent with Buffett's letters. FDIC $250K per depositor per bank per ownership category; no insured losses since 1933; SVB ~$209B assets, ~$42B withdrawn in a day, ~90% uninsured; 157 failures in 2010 - consistent. NBER: 34 recessions since 1854 and ~10-month average post-war recessions correct; average expansion is ~5 years (script "nearly 4") - understated.
